prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a smooth brightness gradient across the round table directly in front of the camera wearer (~0.3 m at the near edge to ~1.1 m at the far edge), flanked by an empty chair on the right (~0.8–1.0 m), another chair behind the far table edge (~1.2–1.4 m), and a seated person on the left (~0.8–1.1 m away, about 0.8 m left of the right chair) before a dark background wall (~2–3 m+). The camera wearer's two hands and the surgical mask held ~0.2–0.4 m in front of the chest are the brightest and nearest elements, positioned above the table surface and a second mask resting below them, while the seated person's crossed arms rest on the left table edge within arm's reach of both people (~0.6–0.8 m from the wearer). Across the five frames, the wearer's hands move slightly away from and toward the lens (~0.25–0.45 m) as they unfold the upper mask, while the seated person on the left shifts slightly rightward into frame 5 (bringing their head and torso more fully into view from the left border) and the held mask partially occludes the table, lower mask, and nearby cell phone. Compared to RGB alone, the depth map clearly separates the vertical height of the held mask and hands above the flat tabletop regardless of harsh sunlight and shadows across the white table. However, the map is unreliable on flat thin objects—blending the two tabletop cell phones and the lower mask completely into the table surface—and treats the transparent glass window and outdoor courtyard behind the table as a uniform black void.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map labels the seated person on the left (~0.8–1.1 m away, partially cut off by the left frame edge in frames 1–4 before shifting rightward in frame 5), the far chair (~1.2–1.4 m ahead), the right chair (~0.8–1.0 m to the right), the round dining table in front of the wearer (~0.3–1.1 m), and two cell phones resting ~0.3 m apart on the tabletop within arm's reach (~0.5–0.7 m from the wearer and ~0.1–0.4 m from the seated person's hands). It also segments the camera wearer's own hands in the lower foreground (~0.2–0.4 m away) as 'person' instances positioned above the table and partially occluding the nearer cell phone and surgical masks across the sequence as the hands spread and lower the right hand in frame 5. The map explicitly isolates the semantic boundaries of the dark cell phones against the shadowed tabletop and darkly clothed arms, which are low-contrast in the RGB frames. However, the segmentation is highly inconsistent and unreliable across time: the round dining table is completely missed in frames 1–3 and only segmented in frames 4–5, neither surgical mask is recognized as a distinct object class (being merged into the wearer's hands, the table, or background), and the left person's torso is mislabeled as part of the dining table in frame 4 and split into multiple person fragments in frame 5.
descriptions.pose: The pose map tracks the 2D skeletal keypoints of the foreground hands and, in the final frame, the upper body of the person seated ~0.8–1.1 m to the left of the camera wearer across the ~1 m table. In frames 1–3, it detects the seated person's left hand resting on the table (~0.7 m from the wearer, within arm's reach of the left cell phone) and only the wearer's right hand (~0.3 m in front of the lens), then adds the wearer's left hand in frame 4 (~0.15 m left of the right hand as both manipulate the mask), while in frame 5 it switches to the seated person's yellow torso/head skeleton and the wearer's two magenta hands below. In frame 5, the yellow facial and shoulder keypoints show the seated person's torso angled toward the table center and their head turned to face and look toward the camera wearer and the held mask as they lean slightly rightward into full view. This skeletal representation makes exact finger articulation, palm orientation, and the seated person's head/gaze direction in the blurred RGB face region immediately explicit without visual clutter from the masks or shadows. However, it is unreliable wherever body parts are partially occluded or near frame borders, completely missing the seated person's body and head in frames 1–4 despite being visible on the left, dropping the wearer's left hand in frames 1–3, and losing the seated person's magenta left-hand skeleton in frame 5.
